builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Surrogate Modeling and Reduced-Order Methods in Gravitational-Wave Physics and Numerical Relativity: From Spectral Representations to Adaptive Compression
summary: The technique replaces direct numerical integration of the Einstein field equations and brute-force Bayesian parameter estimation with projection-based reduced-order models (POD, greedy basis selection, Empirical Interpolation) and reduced-order quadratures that compress waveform solution manifolds into rapidly evaluable surrogates. Its costs are the offline construction of high-fidelity training snapshots, basis computation, and accuracy degradation in regimes with slow Kolmogorov n-width decay, requiring adaptive hp-greedy partitioning and multi-scale compression as mitigation. It can fail in non-stationary, transient, or strongly nonlinear regimes where a fixed global basis cannot represent the solution manifold, and where the surrogate is queried outside its certified training domain.
rationale: The paper addresses surrogate modeling for numerical relativity and gravitational-wave inference, a physics simulation domain with no direct application to LLM production infrastructure.
technique: Reduced-order surrogate modeling for numerical relativity
